name: Mill Creek Alzheimer's Special Care Center

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 gallons of milk held past their expiration date (6/9/26). CORRECTED- items were removed and discarded. Ensure prepackaged foods are not held past their expiration or “best by” dates to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed pork, cooked rice, chicken wings, and 2 opened gallons of milk in the walk in cooler without date marking. CORRECTED- the milk was discarded (see other violation #23), the person in charge (PIC) indicated the foods were prepared yesterday, and marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all ready to eat temperature control for food safety are date marked with the day of preparation (or opening in the case of milk), if being held over 24 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The batteries in the facility’s heat measuring dish puck were observed to be nonoperational. CORRECTED- new batteries were obtained and replaced during today’s inspection. Ensure a temperature measuring device is readily available and used to verify proper temperatures for heat sanitation.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking along the shelf to the right of the dish machine was observed to be in disrepair. Discussed with the PIC- who stated the repair work will occur in the evening to allow the caulking to properly dry. Ensure caulking is replaced by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry of moisture into the equipment.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed green debris on food contact surface-can opener, under the hood vent. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and surface was sanitized. Ensure frequent cleaning and sanitizing of food contact surfaces to prevent build up or contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Accumulation was observed on vent covers above hot holding steam table. Discussed need for routine cleaning and sanitation to prevent contamination of ready to eat food items. Discuss weekly cleaning schedule with staff members.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A jar of jelly and a jar of capers were observed stored on shelving at ambient temperature. Both jars bore labels indicating the need for refrigeration after opening. CORRECTED- Capers and jelly were voluntarily discarded. PIC will discuss storage with staff. Foods should be stored as indicated on their labels.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
A whisk was observed in poor condition, with the coating peeling off of the food contact portions of the whisk. CORRECTED- Whisk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure utensils are cleanable and in good condition.
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No quat sanitizer was observed in a red sanitizer bucket on the cookline. CORRECTED- PIC remade the sanitizer bucket from the 3 compartment sink. Sanitizer was observed at 400ppm quat. PIC mentioned that the bucket was likely just soapy water for cleaning. Ensure chemicals are in labeled (or color-coded) containers to eliminate confusion. Use test strips to monitor sanitizer concentrations.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Three gallons of milk (one opened) observed with a manufacturer use-by date of 1/15. CORRECTED- Three gallons of milk were voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Spatula observed damaged and cracked. CORRECTED- Damaged spatula was voluntarily discarded. Ensure food contact surfaces and utensils are smooth and durable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloth observed on the beverage counter. Store in-use wiping cloths submerged in a sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Employee’s hat observed stored on the handle of the can opener. Store personal items away from food prep areas. Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket used for wiping counters observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Bucket was remade from wall-mounted dispenser. Sanitizer observed at 400ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Leftover mashed potatoes in the walk-in cooler had a date mark of 6/2. The use by date for the product was 6/8. Leftover portion of tomato soup in the walk-in cooler had a date mark of 6/6, making the use by date 6/12. Both items were removed from the walk-in cooler during inspection and discarded. Ensure foods are used or discarded within 7 days.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Can of soup with a severe dent along the top seam was observed in kitchen with other items to be used for dinner prep. Package integrity was discussed. Can in question was discarded and new product was provided.
Food packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was reading around 38F in a cup of ice. Water was added to make ice water slurry for calibration, and thermometer was adjusted for calibration at 32F. Thermometer was previously used to check the cook temperature of hamburger. Ensure calibration of thermometers prior to checking food temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee working with manager at time of inspection had a food handler certification that expired in October 2021. Employee is scheduled to take a food manager course for certification at the end of the month. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer solution in cook line sani-bucket was observed at 0ppm quat. New solution was dispensed and once again observed at 0ppm with inspector’s instant change test strip and facility’s litmus paper test strip. Sanitizer was not dispensing properly due to the development of an air bubble in the chemical line. PIC disconnected and adjusted the chemical line to correct the issue. Solution in sani-bucket was observed at 200ppm after troubleshooting. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC at the time of inspection has a food handler certification. PIC took a food manager course and needs to take the exam to obtain CFM. Kitchen manager had the day off and was called in during the inspection. Ensure that all people who have the potential to be the PIC have a current food manager certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Butcher knife in the knife storage rack had food debris stuck on the blade. Knife was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 
--Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris from prior use that day. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitization of equipment food contact surface and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed along the bottom edge of the baffle in the ice machine. Monthly detail cleaning of the machine occurred recently. Ensure surfaces in the bin and on the baffle are cleaned and sanitized as needed between monthly cleaning and disinfection of the machine. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket on cook line was observed at 0ppm quat. PIC stated the solution was just prepared. A new solution was dispensed and once again was observed at 0ppm. Once chemical dispenser was allowed to run for several seconds sanitizer began to suction through the line, and the new solution was observed at 200ppm quat. Previous solutions were likely diluted from water that was dispensed prior to chemical suctioning through the line. Ensure sanitizer is coming through the chemical line prior to filling sani-buckets. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 Final rinse temperature of the dish machine entering at the manifold was observed to be 196F-197F. In the meantime, when the dish machine sat unused for several minutes the final rinse temperature at the manifold went down to 195F. Maintenance was advised as to the issue and will make necessary adjustments per the manual to ensure a final rinse temp of no greater than 194F. The dish machine is scheduled to be replaced in the next quarter.
In a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Upon arrival of inspector, PIC had a mint in his mouth while working in the kitchen. Proper consumption of food, including gum and candy, was discussed. Mint was fully consumed prior to continuing with tasks.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee was observed entering the kitchen and did not wash hands prior to handling a clean spoon and aluminum foil. Employee made his way to the handsink to wash hands prior to putting on gloves and was advised hands need to be washed immediately upon entering the kitchen and before handling anything related to food service. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Ensure hands are washing upon entering the work area and before handling anything related to food service.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade had debris stuck on it. Can opener was last used during the previous operating day. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize the can opener between uses.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked noodles were observed in a pan covered with plastic wrap in the far right holding well of the steam table. The holding well was off, and food employee stated the noodles were just cooked and cooled under cold running water within the half hour. Internal temperature was observed at 58F-59F for noodles. Options for rapid chilling were discussed including ice baths and storage in the walkin cooler until ready for use. The plastic wrap was loosened along one edge and product labeled prior to placing in the walkin cooler for storage until ready to be reheated to 165F/above for lunch service. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.15 & 4-501.110 Dish machine wash temperature did not get to 150F during inspection. After running ~8 to 9 times the wash temperature read at 116F. The final rinse temperature readout showed 192F, and dish machine testers verified final rinse temperature was over 160F. The wash temperature slowly climbed over time and was observed at 129F after consistent use of the machine for well over 30 minutes. A leak in the machine may have caused issues with the circuit board, which was covered on the inner surface of the mechanical panel with a garbage bag. The temperature log showed wash temperatures consistently below 150F. Manager was advised to call for service. In the meantime, the wash step for dishes will occur at the 3 part sink prior to placing items in the dish machine for heat sanitization. 
The temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers that use hot water to sanitize may not be less than 150F for a stationary rack, dual temperature machine.
A warewashing machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Jackets were observed hanging on shelving in dry storage area. Jackets were removed from the shelving.
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions. Consider over the door hangers or installing hooks on the door or in the back hallway to remedy the storage of personal items.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Metal stem of food temperature was soiled with grease and food debris. Alcohol wipe was used to clean off the stem during inspection. Cleaning/sanitizing and general maintenance of food thermometers were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Can opener blade had debris on it. Can opener was placed through a ware washing cycling in the dish machine during inspection.
Clean and sanitize the can opener between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Food employee was observed touching the manual faucet with his hand to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Proper handwashing technique poster was observed at the handsink and used for reference. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed going between tasks and then put on a pair of gloves without first washing hands. Employee wiped down surfaces with towel from a sani-bucket and put on oven mitts to remove food from the oven prior to putting on gloves. Proper handwashing between tasks and prior to donning gloves were discussed. Employee were observed washing hands between tasks for the remainder of the inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands and prior to putting on gloves..

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Box of raw back was observed on top of a box with deli meat and hotdogs in the walkin cooler. Foods were rearranged for proper storage of raw food below ready to eat. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener blade was soiled with food buildup. Can opener had not been used up to that point during the  current operating day. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection.

Clean and sanitize the can opener between uses and at maximum up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open package of deli meat was observed without a date mark. Product was opened on 7/20 per the menu for the month. Date was provided. Manager stated the deli meat would be used by the end of the day or discarded based on the 7 day time frame for use. Also, an open package of hotdogs without a date mark was observed in the walkin cooler. Hotdogs were discarded.
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Boxes of bread were observed on the floor in the walkin freezer. Delivery was received the day prior. Staff were advised to provide a means to elevate the food off the floor. Staff stated the products would be rearranged in the freezer to allow for proper storage later today. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to measure the surface temperature at the dish rack to verify proper heat sanitization during a ware washing cycle. Options for measuring the final rinse temperature were discussed. Provide a means to measure the final rinse temperature at the surface of dishes. (See general comments for additional information)
In hot water mechanical ware washing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.
Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener was observed with buildup along the edge of the blade. Can opener was last used at breakfast and was taken to dish area to go through ware washing.
Knife storage rack had an accumulation of dust and crumbs on top. Storage rack and all knives were taken to the dish area to go through ware washing. 

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses. Clean storage areas for clean equipment, such as knife racks, as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Coat was observed hanging on the dry storage shelving next to food and single service items. Coat was removed from the area.

Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Worker just washed his hands and was observed drying hands with paper towels. The paper towels were then used to shut of the faucet of the handsink before continuing to dry hands with the same paper towels. Handwashing technique was discussed. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food and clean equipment.
NOTE: The point of using the paper towel as a barrier to shut off the faucet is to avoid recontamination of freshly washed hands. New paper towels are needed to finish drying hands once paper towels are used to shut off the manual faucet.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
(R) 750.830 - A serving spoon, ladle, spatula, and food shears were observed in the clean utensil storage area and were soiled with stuck on food debris/general buildup. All items were removed from the area to go through ware washing process again. 

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
NOTE: Repeat the process as many times as needed to remove all gross soil from all surfaces of equipment during ware washing to ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Kitchen staff scheduled to work the afternoon shift had food handler certifications. None of the staff with food manager certifications were on the schedule to work, and the Kitchen Manager was on vacation. The employee who worked the morning shift and has a current manager certification was called back in to work the afternoon shift and oversee food prep/service. Director noted more kitchen staff will be getting food manager certifications. 

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of certified food managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  certified food managers.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Knife in the storage rack had a piece of food debris stuck on the blade. It appeared the knife went through ware washing without all food debris being removed. Knife was removed for cleaning.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation. Repeat the process as many times as needed to remove all gross soil from all surfaces of equipment during ware washing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets were observed at 0ppm quat. Both were made earlier in the morning. Both were remade and observed at 200ppm quat. Maintain sani-buckets at 150-400ppm (per instructions on product label), and change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and/or wiping cloths become heavily soiled.
**Make sure all employees know and understand the proper way to fill sani-buckets from the chemical dispenser. The solution comes out at the concentration needed, so water should not be added when filling buckets from the dispenser.**

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) coffee machine spout above grounds basket (buildup); and
B) top of knife rack (dust and debris).

Clean and sanitize the above food contact surfaces at least up to every 24hrs if not more frequently depending on use and buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1060 - Water was once again observed leaking from the lower edge of the garbage grinder. Manager noted the garbage grinder was replaced since the previous inspection but thought there might be a leak at the gasket. Heavy condensation was noted in the area and was wiped off with fresh dry cloths. After removing condensation, a leak was observed on the left side of the garbage grinder. Maintenance was made aware of the issue during the inspection.
 
All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
(R) 750.510 - Proper handwashing technique was not used by one employee prior to putting on gloves to handle clean utensils. Employee rinsed hands and did not lather with soap, and the process did not last 20 seconds. 
Another employee was observed shutting off the faucet without a proper barrier; employee used his thumb to shut off the faucet. Proper handwashing was discussed with both employees. Staff were later observed washing hands with proper technique.
***Employees must properly wash their hands every time they wash at the handsink. Properly wash hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
 (Educational handout on proper technique provided)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800b - Pink and black mold was observed starting to accumulate inside the ice machine on the lower edge of the removable baffle. The baffle was placed through a ware washing cycle in the dish machine. Once the baffle was removed it was possible to see conditions inside on the ceiling around where the ice comes out. Black mold and some lime buildup were observed on the ceiling in side the machine. Kitchen supervisor cleaned inside the ice machine during the inspection.
***Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine and the removable baffle as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and lime.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Utensil storage drawer and those beneath it used for storage of activity supplies were soiled with splash and general buildup. Supervisor stated the drawers will be cleaned this evening. Supervisor was advised to have the person in charge of activities properly clean and sanitize items used for food service prior to placing trays, slicers, etc. back in the storage drawers.
***Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Water was observed leaking from the lower edge of the garbage grinder. Properly repair the garbage grinder so it does not leak on the floor.
***All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: See 7/3/17 routine inspection report for details

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120 & 250 - Box of meatballs and a package of raw ground beef were observed on a cart at ambient temperature upon arrival of inspector. The meatballs were still frozen; the ground beef had a surface temperature ranging from 62F-64F. Both products were moved to the walkin cooler for storage until cook was ready to prepare meat sauce for the evening meal.  NOTE: The internal temperature of the ground beef was checked about 5 minutes after it was placed back in the cooler and was observed at 44F. Cook was advised to leave foods in the cooler until they are needed for prep to minimize the amount of time foods are in the temperature danger zone.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Several ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods were opened and observed without date marks. Foods included deli meats (turkey & bologna), American cheese, boiled eggs, and a gallon of milk. Cook on duty was unsure as to when the cheese, deli meats, and milk were opened but was certain the turkey, cheese, and milk were opened within the last day or two. The bologna was discarded, while the cheese, turkey and milk were dated and kept for use. The boiled eggs were just opened to prepare a salad for dinner service and were dated as well. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous, ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be served or discarded. maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with cook. Hands were re-washed with proper technique prior to continuing with food prep.

Hands must be properly washed any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket had a concentration of 0ppm quat. A new sanitizer solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm. Sanitizing concentration was discussed, and proper use of test strips was demonstrated.

Change sani-bucket solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. 
Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) can opener - blade & crevice around the blade (debris and metal shavings) - taken to dish area to go through ware washing;   and
B) ice machine - lower edge of baffle (mold) & edge of ceiling behind the lid (dust).

Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Cook working at the time of inspection had a food handler certification. No other staff with a current food manager certification were working at the time of inspection. (See General Comments)

Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151(a) - Open package of American cheese was observed without a date mark. Manager noted the product was dated the day it was received on 2/9 and was thought to have been opened on 2/12. Based on information provided the cheese was past the 7 day time frame for use. Cheese was discarded in the trash during inspection.
Discussed option of freezing food portions to eliminate potential food waste. Make sure the dates foods are frozen and pulled for use/thawed are tracked accordingly to ensure foods are used or discarded within a total to 7 days.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g -. Facility did not have quat test kit for checking sanitizer concentration. Manager noted he just ran out and would be placing an order for test strips this week.  

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
750.830f - Ladles and tongs hanging in clean storage area were observed with debris on food contact surfaces. Ladles may have been soiled by incidental splash during breakfast prep. However, tongs were soiled with stuck on grease and appeared to have gone through ware washing process and placed back in storage area without being properly cleaned and sanitized. Ladles and tongs were taken to dish area to go through ware washing process again. Manager was advised to pre-soak items and repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure all gross food debris/soil is removed from utensils and equipment.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee switch tasks from handling soiled tray of dishes to handling clean dishes without properly washing hands between tasks. Discussed hand washing during the inspection. Employee properly washed hands throughout the remainder of the inspection. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the fans in the walk-in cooler (dust); 2) the edge of the drawers on the long preparation counter (food crumbs); 3) the fan on the floor by the oven (dusty); and 4) the side of the ice machine (splash). Clean the non-food contact surfaces. All non-food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b) Observed hamburgers resting on the counter in a covered container. Food was temped at 89F. Container did not have a time indicated on the exterior. During the inspection, hamburgers were uncovered and the time was indicated on the label (foods were just pulled from grill after lunch service). See notes in the General Comments. Make sure that cooling is conducted quickly (place uncovered in freezer or cooler) and that the time is indicated on the food. Monitor the food to insure that time/temperature benchmarks are being met.  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment: 750-830  The heat sanitizing dish machine is not reaching 180F. Machine's wash temperature is reaching 155F, the final rinse, however, is only reaching around 122F. A thermo-strip was run through the machine and did not change temperature. Will follow-up on repairs in one week. In the interim, use the dish machine for washing and rinsing and then sanitize the dishes in the three compartment sink. Make sure that staff knows to submerged the dishes into the sanitizing solution for at least sixty seconds. All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dish washing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800b: Observed the baffle of the ice machine to have slight mold accumulation. The ice is currently near full within the basin. When the ice volume is at its lowest, make sure the baffle surface is wiped with a sani-cloth. Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces as frequently as necessary to maintain the surfaces clean.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed a pepper to have mold. The pepper was discarded during the inspection. Food must be in sound condition.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the coffee spout soiled. 2) Observed the can opener blade to have some debris accumulation. Clean the food contact surfaces. The coffee spout was cleaned during the inspection.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed some liquid spillage on a dry storage shelf. The shelving was cleaned during the inspection. Make sure to clean non-food contact surfaces as needed.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the underside of the coffee spout to have accumulated ground debris and the baffle of the ice machine to have minor mold accumulation. The coffee machine was cleaned during the inspection. Clean the baffle of the ice machine after ice count is low enough not to put hand in contact with product during cleaning. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed personal drinks in various places around the kitchen (Jones soda on second to bottom shelf in walk-in cooler, by mixer in kitchen, on counter by can-opener). No food preparation was occurring during the inspection.  Drinks were moved. Designate a spot (low and away) for employee beverage storage. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the sani-bucket for the cookline to be at 0ppm Quat. Bucket was in use from this morning. Emptied and filled during inspection. Monitor sani-buckets and change as needed to innsure 200ppm Quat. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floor drains are observed soiled. Clean the floor drains (especially under ice machine and prep sink). Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 The hood is soiled with grease accumulation around the edges. Wipe down the hood to prevent grease leaks from falling onto clean dishes.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
750-140(b) Observed a covered, 8" container of peas to now have a time indicated on the covering. The peas were observed in the wallk in cooler at 86F. Date on the peas indicated 1/28/15. During the inspection, cooling was discussed. Peas were removed and properly vented with proper date and time indicated on them. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

Indicate the time on the cooling foods to insure that temperature benchmarks are being met. If something over 135F is pulled from hot holding then you may choose to store it on the counter for a brief period as it cools to 135F. Cooling in a commercial kitchen is an active process. Help the food lose heat as quickly as possible.  Cooling foods should be left uncovered and in shallow pans. You may choose to use an ice bath, an ice wand or even store the food in the freezer for awhile in order to help cooler. Make sure the time is indicated on the cooling food. Once the food has cooled, cover.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: 750-230 Observed a single stem thermometer in the knife block to be reading the ambient temperature of 35F. The two in-use thermometers were also not indicating an accurate ambient temperature. Calibration of the three thermometers was checked during the inspection. All three thermometers were placed in a cup of ice and water. Temperature readings on all three were under, seriously under, or slightly over the desired 32F. There is not a sleeve and wrench present to aide in adjusting the thermometers. Manager is going to finish calibrating the stems later as a proper tool is acquired. A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Observed tongs stored with clean utensils to have full pieces of chicken stuck in the grooves. Properly remove gross food accumulation prior to or as part of the ware washing process. Make sure that gross food is removed so that the large pieces do not sit at room temperature and then mix with fresh food being handled. Tongs were pulled for cleaning during the inspection. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee using the same gloves to handle all manner of soiled utensils, equipment, buckets, and then handle clean plates. The issue of needing to change gloves prior to handling clean dishes was raised on two separate occasions before gloves were removed. The potential to spread diseases from patient-to-patient during this flu season is extreme when handling multiple soiled plates and then immediately handling the clean ones. Change gloves and wash hands frequently between the handling of soiled items and sanitized items. Discussed glove necessity with manager. Gloves need not be worn when handling clean plates, HOWEVER, hands must be properly washed between tasks. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a A spatula with a ripped top was observed stored with clean utensils. The spatula was discarded during the inspection. Periodically check utensils to insure surfaces are in sound repair. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b The sani-buckets holding wet wiping cloths are observed at 0ppm Quat. During the inspection, all the buckets were emptied. Sanitizing solution is dispensing at 200ppm Quat. The kitchen also has a bottle for disinfecting. This disinfectant is 400ppm Quat. Please discuss the difference of these two concentration with staff so they are aware of when to use the different concentrations.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) The underside spout of the coffee machine (remove the grounds basket) and the wall-mounted knife block are observed soiled with accumulated food debris. Clean the coffee spout and the knife block. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The over drip tray and the top shelf holding spices is observed soiled with food debris. The oven drip tray is loaded with old food spills. The top shelf of the spice rack is soiled with grease splash and dust.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Observed the top shelf over the preparation line/utensil storage area to have pitchers and containers not properly inverted. Flip containers or store them on a lower shelf so the food contact surface is protected. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed coffee filters to not be properly covered. They are being stored on the counter adjacent to the coffee machine. Store filters so they are protected from overhead contamination and food splash. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Cheese slices observed in the walk-in fridge without a date marking label. Cheese slices are from a previous day. Label all opened potentially hazardous foods at the end of the evening or find another routine that satisfies this Food Code requirement. Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed a styrofoam cup being used as a scoop in the bulk sugar container. Pulled from use during inspection. Use a scoop with a proper handle so bare hand does not contact possible ready-to-eat foods. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed an opened plastic cupof water being stored on the second to top shelf of the clean dish rack by the dish machine. Cup of water was observed on same tray as clean cups. Discussed storage of personal beverages. Use a disposable cup with a lid and a straw and the ccup may be located adjacent to your work space. An opened glass, bottle or can must be stored adjacent to the handsink so that hands are washed after each sip. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the quat sani-bucket at 0ppm residual. Emptied and filled during inspection. Concentration in solution indicated 200ppm Quat.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floor drain beneath the ice machine to be soiled with mold. Clean the floor drain.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed ground beef cooling in a covered container without a time indicated on the product. Beef was observed (probed) at 81F. During the inspection, the container was uncovered and the time the food was placed within the walk-in cooler was written on the plasticwrap. When cooling hot foods make sure that the time the food is placed within the cooler is recorded somehow (either on the actual container or on a ledger or dry erase board). Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed a small plastic glass of ice water stored on a counter adjacent to coffee filters, gloves, hot cocoa packets, and various other kitchen items. During the inspection the glass was emptied and moved to the dishmachine for cleaning. Discussed location of employee beverages. Disposable cups with lid and straw may be kept at your work station.Washable glasses need to be kept on a low shelf and near a handwashing sink so hands may be properly washed after contact. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120e The satellite kitchen is not supplied with paper towels. Supply this handsink with towels and soap. A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d)  Raw beef was observed over cooked roast beef in the walk-in cooler. Items were on a rollcart and were trayed seperately. Properly stored during inspection. Also, kitchen receives a number of items from resident's families for service to the residents. These foods are seperately stored within a tub. Store foods on the lowest shelf in the walk-in freezer and indicate contents of the tub using 'PERSONAL'. All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160: Observed a cup being used as a scoop within the bulk sugar container. Removed from use during the inspection. Facility has proper scoops available in other bulk containers. Make sure these proper scoops are used when scooping.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d) Observed two different boxes of eggs being stored over chocolate shakes and potato salad in the walk-in cooler. During the inspection the items were properly stored under the ready-to-eat foods. Gave a storage handout to manager. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a Observed employee beverages stored on a food preparation counter. During inspection, drinks were stored on managers desk. Designate where employees should place their drinks. Employees need to stay hydrated, but treat drinking moment as a break. Break, drink, wash hands, and return to task. Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floor drains beneath the ice machine and the dish machine to be soiled with accumulated soil and food debris - especially the ice machine (black mold growth observed). During the inspection, the drains were being cleaned.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors. ALSO, there is a fabric mat observed in front of the ice machine. Replace this fabric mat with one that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280: Observed coats and purses stored on the racks of the dry storage room. Manager stated that their are lockers available at the front of the facility. If possible, provide hooks for staff to hang coats around manager's desk. During inspection, all coats and personal belongings were stored on a chair next to the manager's desk.
